recipes.name: Starr’s Savory Meatballs
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup dry bread crumbs, or as needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

Mix ground beef, onion, bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, eggs, garlic, oregano, basil, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until just combined. Divide mixture into 4 equal portions; roll each portion into 4 meatballs. Arrange meatballs on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the centers, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Starr’s Savory Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: Starr’s savory meatball recipe combines ground beef, bread crumbs, egg, Parmesan cheese, Worcestershire sauce, and three herbs — thyme, oregano, basil.

review.reviewBody: Out of dry bread crumbs at the moment, I used crushed garlic croutons instead. I made no other changes. GREAT meatballs. Excellent for meatball sandwiches.

These were perfect for sub sandwiches! We tweaked them by browning them stovetop first, then we put them in a baking dish lined with marinara, topped the meatballs with marinara, shredded Parmesan, and mozzarella. They baked for about 45 minutes and fit right into French hoagie, all saucy and cheesy! Definitely added to our regular monthly dinner menu!

Made this simple recipe for family and friends, everyone loved them! Perfect, this will be my forever go-to recipe for meatballs. I agree with other reviews, chop onions finer and use less oregano. Also, I'll try the suggestion to brown them in skillet before baking.

Very nice tasting meatballs, and I'm not a fan of them. Herby, yes, and maybe a tad salty, depending on what you are doing with them. I followed the recipe precisely 'cept for using a few dehydrated onions rather than fresh. Remember to wear a glove on your mixing hand so you don't get "garlicked" and I thought a med size cookie scoop was perfect for our family (3 small kids). The other thing I'll do next time is to pluck the meatballs off the parchment when they come out and let them sit for a minute on a paper towel. There was plenty for dinner, left overs, and a few to freeze for a separate meal. This was easy, quick to prepare and leave in the fridge until dinner time and left overs were gone within 24 hours, so the recipe was a keeper.

Good meatballs; used for subs. I felt the portions were HUGE, double my typical portion anyhow, so I ended up freezing half. I had even halved the recipe! I think you could get 8 servings if served in sandwiches or over spaghetti out of 2 lbs of ground meat. I used ground turkey and added more Worcestershire b/c I think it helps 'beef' up the flavor when using ground turkey in recipes calling for beef (I find it makes turkey less noticeable to the usual beef-eaters). I made the meatballs a bit smaller than directed, and they were perfectly cooked after 15 minutes. Good balance of the onion, garlic and spices. Thank you!

I just made these tonight (late), but they came out just wonderful. Our family loves garlic so I did add a couple more cloves. They looked like they needed a couple more minutes in the oven so I flipped them over after 15 mins. & gave them 10 more. Then I dropped them into a pot of spaghetti sauce with the intention of having meatball subs, but because of the late hour, we just ate a meatball with sauce on the place and it was fantastic! Can't wait to have them on a sub roll tomorrow night! Thanks Starr!

These were good, but a bit bland. Next time I might try 1 lb of ground beef and 1 lb of ground sausage.

I also used a 2" ice cream scoop to divide the beef.
Too much oregano. I recommend using 1/2 the amount because the tablespoon of oregano made the meatballs too aromatic - almost minty tasting.

Used 1 1/2 lbs ground beef and 1/2 lb hot sausage. I would recommend dicing onions very small as mine were a bit too large. Very greasy....I had to wipe each one off and the pan was a pond of grease. I think next time I'll bake them on a wire rack on top of the cookie sheet. Next time I will reduce the thyme as it kind of overwhelms the other flavors. Good base recipe that can easily be adapted to your liking.
These are fanatastic! I made these with spagetthi and fried the meatballs in oil before simmering them in the pasta sauce. So good!

As an Allrecipe's Allstar, I was given a challenge to replace ground beef in a favorite recipe with Johnsonville brand sausage. I swapped ground mild Italian Johnsoville sausage and it was quite a success! These meatballs were crispy on the outside and very moist, juicy, and full of flavor on the inside! This was such a simple swap that imparted some new flavor into a favorite recipe, I will definitely try this again!
!st couple of bites, my husband said, "Wow, I like these meatballs." This will be my go to recipe from now on. Thanks for sharing it.
We use this recipe all the time for spaghetti and sandwiches with leftovers. thank you Starr!
Smells amazing! I made it just now and I cannot wait to fast it!
FANTASTIC RECIPE - VERY TASTY!!!!
This is fabulous as written. No changes needed . I cannot recommend anything to make it better. Perfect as written. This goes into a regular meal rotation. Thanks for sharing
Not the best meat balls. If the breading was left out, it would have been better.
Delicious! I made the meatballs bite size (per another reviewers suggestion!) and put them in the oven for five minutes. I made them as spaghetti and meatballs and my family loved it!
I made as the recipe stated. Too strong on the herb flavors for me, and it needs a little salt when done cooking.

These are definitely delicious! I made them with ground pork and I had to substitute provolone and mozzarella cheeses because I had no parmesan. Made the rotini pasta and marinara sauce the highlight of a week night meal!
Thank you Starr for submitting these meatballs.
